transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-08
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~44 minutes (recording ended ~16:14 UTC)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Lantern CTO), Ethan (Head of ML), Amir (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Lantern is preparing a renewal for Q3 that includes an APAC burst and wants to explore a Private VPC pilot for EU sensitive workloads. Questions around latency targets, KMS/SAML, and contract cadence. Redwood proposed a staged approach (burst -> dedicated reserve -> private pilot).

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving this time out. Super quick, Priya, Ethan, Amir — thanks. We wanted to run through the renewal ask and the APAC burst readout. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Liam from SE.
[00:12] Priya: Thanks Maya. Yeah, we wanted to cover three things — the capacity uplift numbers, how fast we can get APAC nodes live, and then a private pilot conversation for EU PHI-ish data.
[00:25] Liam: Cool, and I'll jump into the benchmark plan and the technical constraints. Quick note, transcript might mangle some product names, you'll see Redwood Optimize come out as Redwood Optmise sometimes.
[00:36] Ethan: (chuckles) that'll be the day — as long as the numbers are right.
[00:40] Amir: Quick operational note: our infra egress caps in ap-southeast-1 are 6 Gbps per cluster; anything above that we need a prior ticket with our cloud provider.
[00:49] Maya: Great, good to know. Okay, Lance... Lantern sorry, Lantern's ask was — 2x token throughput during APAC peak window, roughly a 6-week campaign starting mid-April with a possible extension. They want to know options: quick burst (hosted/dedicated burst) vs reserved capacity, plus a side private VPC pilot in EU for compliance.
[01:10] Priya: Correct. Also want to keep per-token cost close to our current baseline. We can't triple unit costs.
[01:16] Liam: Understood. For the APAC burst there are two simple paths: 1) short-term dedicated burst nodes — we can provision pools and autoscale, or 2) hosted but routed through our apac nodes — the latter is faster to start but less isolated. Both have fallback policies we can set. The dedicated burst gives you predictable throughput and you can set per-route throttles.
[01:38] Ethan: What's the expected latency delta for dedicated burst vs hosted in APAC? We're sensitive to 50–100 ms tail latencies on small prompts.
[01:48] Liam: In our experience, dedicated nodes in ap-southeast can shave 20–40ms off median token latency for the same model family versus a global hosted pool, because of lower network hops and reserved GPU scheduling. But it depends on sequence length and batching. If you have heavy batching it can push latency up, so we recommend continuous batching tuning for chat workloads.
[02:09] Priya: And region provisioning lead time?
[02:12] Maya: Operationally we can do a short warm-up (3–5 business days) for a burst pool in APAC if we have the model pinned and the commit. If it's a new private VPC in EU, that takes longer — typically 3–4 weeks for security review, KMS integration, and peering.
[02:29] Amir: That timeline's ok. For the private pilot we need to validate KMS key wrapping and HSM options — we currently use Vault plus external HSM for critical keys. How does Redwood handle customer-managed keys?
[02:41] Liam: For Private deployments we support external KMS/HSM integrations via standard envelope encryption. You provide the key material or the KMS endpoint; Redwood will not store plaintext keys. There are audit log hooks and we can include key-usage logs in the console. Note: there can be a small throughput impact if you call KMS synchronously on every request, so we recommend caching key tokens and local wrapping for high-throughput paths.
[03:03] Priya: Okay that sounds fine, we just need the KMS provider compatibility list.
[03:07] Maya: We'll include that in the security pack.
[03:09] Ethan: On the benchmarking side, what's the plan? We're going to run our prompt set, but we want to be sure the KV cache behavior (you know, prefix caching) is similar to prod.
[03:20] Liam: Plan: Liam runs two runs — one on hosted APAC nodes and one on dedicated burst nodes with your payload. We'll use your 10 representative prompts and a 30-minute steady-state run and a 5-minute spike test. I'll capture tail p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll also validate KV cache hit rates.
[03:40] Ethan: Sounds good. We'll push the prompts after this call.
[03:43] Priya: A quick question on fallback: if the dedicated pool saturates, what's the automatic behavior? Do requests queue? Do they fail over to global hosted?
[03:52] Liam: You can choose policy. Typical setup is automatic fallback to a compatible lower-tier model in the hosted pool with a configurable threshold, plus queueing up to X seconds. We can also set a hard reject. We'll propose a canary fallback (route 5% to hosted) while enabling autoscale/burst capacity.
[04:10] Amir: For billing how do you want to structure the short burst? We prefer not to do long-term reserved pricing until we see actuals.
[04:18] Maya: Common approach: a time-limited reserved pool with a short-term commitment (6 weeks) at a blended price — higher than annual committed pricing but lower than on-demand. Then if you convert to reserved capacity later, we can credit the burst usage against the commitment. We'll put that in the amendment.
[04:33] Priya: Okay, that's acceptable. We need clarity on the crediting mechanism.
[04:37] Maya: We'll include worked examples in the contract amendment so you can see the unit economics.
[04:41] Speaker 1: Uh, do we have any security exceptions for third-party logging?
[04:44] Liam: We can restrict telemetry; audit logs can be routed to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 with KMS encryption. We also provide token-level cost breakdowns but can mask payloads.
[04:56] Ethan: Quick note: we want to run a small quality eval during the burst to ensure generation quality doesn't regress due to quantized model profiles. How do we handle model variants?
[05:06] Liam: You can pin to a verified model variant; if you crop quantized variants for cost we recommend an eval set. Redwood Optimize will flag regressions and you can set rollback policies. There might be name mangling in my notes — Redwood Optimize = Redwood Optmise in the transcript.
[05:20] Priya: Who's the contact on the SE side for the benchmark?
[05:23] Maya: That's Liam. I'll hand it to him for timing.
[05:25] Liam: I'll get an invite for next Tuesday/Wednesday window. Amir, I need your egress limits and a test subnet for peering. Also the short list of prompts from Ethan.
[05:35] Amir: I'll drop a doc in the shared folder with CIDRs and KMS provider details by Friday. One ask — can you support SAML SSO with our internal IdP (Azure AD)? We want RBAC tied to Okta/Azure groups.
[05:47] Maya: Absolutely. We support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning. We'll share the SSO integration guide and a sample SSO cert.
[05:55] Priya: On contract cadence: we'd like a 12-month extension but with an opt-out window after 90 days if performance doesn't meet metrics. Is that feasible?
[06:04] Maya: We can do a 12-month term with a performance SLA addendum that includes an early-exit clause tied to agreed metrics — e.g., p95 tail latency and availability. Legal will need to sign off, but we've done similar language before.
[06:16] Ethan: We also want a playbook for graceful degradation — e.g., if model variant fails, fallback to smaller model without hallucination increase. How are hallucinations measured?
[06:25] Liam: We usually tie hallucination/regression monitoring to a test set and evaluate an F1/precision metric on entity-level outputs. We'll propose a set of prompt-based regression checks during the pilot.
[06:35] Priya: Any competitor updates we should be aware of? We're still POC-ing OctaneAI but their APAC footprint is thin. CloudMorph pitched a geo-provisioning product but no KMS story.
[06:45] Maya: Yep noted. We'll provide a short competitive appendix but focus on the operational tradeoffs.
[06:51] Priya: OK. Next steps recap?
[06:54] Maya: Recap: Maya will send a redlined renewal + amendment for APAC burst by Mar 11. Liam will run benchmarks in APAC with your prompts and share results by Mar 12. Amir to share egress/CIDR and KMS provider by Mar 10. Priya/Ethan to confirm pilot scope and metrics by Mar 15.
[07:10] Ethan: We'll get prompts to you in the next 24–48 hours.
[07:13] Amir: I'll upload infra constraints today.
[07:15] Liam: Quick note on instrumentation — we'll give you a dashboard template for p95/p99, tokens/sec, KV cache hit rate, and cost per million tokens.
[07:25] Priya: That will be useful.
[07:26] Maya: Anything else?
[07:28] Speaker 2: One last thing — how does data residency work if we run inference in APAC but log in EU?
[07:33] Liam: You can configure routing: inference can run in APAC, but logs and telemetry can be routed to EU storage. For Private deployments you have full control; for hosted we support log partitioning and redaction.
[07:45] Priya: OK thanks. If there are no further items we'll wrap.
[07:49] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the contract and benchmark invite.
[07:54] End of recording (approx 16:14 UTC).
